_note: Original advanced lesson. Uses language-specific block variants where syntax differs.
title: Binary Search
summary: **Binary search** works when the search space is sorted or has a clear true/false boundary.
refresher: **Binary search** cuts the search space in half each step. It needs sorted data or a monotonic condition. After checking mid, move past mid so the range gets smaller.

advanced-bs-sorted.title: Binary search needs order
advanced-bs-sorted.body: Ordinary **binary search** only works when smaller **values** are on one side and larger values are on the other.
advanced-bs-sorted.notice: The comparison at mid tells you which half can be ignored.
advanced-bs-sorted.mistake: On unsorted data, mid tells you almost nothing.

advanced-bs-mid.title: Mid is the test point
advanced-bs-mid.body: Mid is the **index** in the middle of the current low-to-high range.
advanced-bs-mid.notice: Mid changes as the range shrinks.
advanced-bs-mid.mistake: Do not keep checking the same mid forever.

advanced-bs-stuck.title: Move past mid
advanced-bs-stuck.body: When mid is not the answer, remove it from the remaining range.
advanced-bs-stuck.mistake: `low = mid` can get stuck when low and mid are the same.

sections.title: Search inside low and high
sections.summary: Low and high mark the range still worth checking.

blocks.body: **Binary search** is not just a faster loop. It is a promise: because the data is ordered, one comparison can rule out half of the remaining positions.

blocks.title: Cut the search space
blocks.caption: Watch low, mid, and high move while searching a sorted **list**.

steps.title: Start with the full range
steps.body: low and high cover every possible **index**.

steps.title: Check mid
steps.body: mid points to 9. The target is 15, so 9 is too small.

steps.title: Move low right
steps.body: Everything at mid and left of mid is too small, so discard it.

steps.title: Check new mid
steps.body: mid points to 15, which matches the target.

blocks.title: Closed-range variables
items: `low <= high` keeps a one-item range searchable.

blocks.caption: Find a target in sorted numbers.

blocks.title: C++ runner note
blocks.body: Many CS Navigator C++ practice **functions** use `std::vector<long long>` so large **integer** tests are safe. The **binary search** idea is the same as with `int`.

sections.title: Move past mid
sections.summary: The range must shrink on every **loop**.

blocks.body: If `nums[mid]` is too small, everything at mid and to the left is too small. Move `low` to `mid + 1`. If `nums[mid]` is too large, move `high` to `mid - 1`.

blocks.title: Avoid the stuck-mid bug
blocks.caption: Watch why `low = mid` can repeat the same range instead of shrinking it.

steps.title: Two items remain
steps.body: low is 0, high is 1, and mid becomes 0.
steps.what_changed: The range is tiny, so a bad update can get stuck fast.

steps.title: Wrong update
steps.body: 10 is too small, but setting low to mid keeps low at 0.
steps.what_changed: Nothing moved. The next **loop** checks mid 0 again.

steps.title: Correct update
steps.body: Move past mid because mid was already ruled out.
steps.what_changed: The remaining range now contains only **index** 1.

steps.title: One item can still match
steps.body: `low <= high` lets the final candidate be checked.
steps.what_changed: The target is found instead of skipped.

blocks.caption: Move past **values** you already ruled out.
blocks.body: When `low == mid`, setting `low = mid` changes nothing.

blocks.title: Trace target 9 in [2, 4, 6, 9, 12]
items: 6 is too small, so low becomes 3.

blocks.prompt: In ascending order, `nums[mid]` is less than the target. What should move?
blocks.why: The left side is too small, including mid, so low moves right past mid.

sections.title: Binary search beyond arrays
sections.summary: You can **binary search** an answer range when true/false changes once.

blocks.body: **Binary search** can also work when you are searching for the smallest value that passes a test, or the largest value that still works. The key word is monotonic: once the answer becomes true, it stays true, or once it becomes false, it stays false.

blocks.title: Examples of monotonic questions
items: Smallest speed that finishes on time.
Smallest capacity that can ship all packages.

blocks.title: No boundary, no binary search
blocks.body: If true and false **values** are mixed randomly, the mid result cannot tell you which side to discard.

sections.title: Practice handoff
sections.summary: Write the range meaning before the **loop**.

blocks.body: Before coding **binary search**, write one sentence: `low` and `high` cover the possible answer range. That sentence helps you choose `<=`, `mid + 1`, and `mid - 1` correctly.

blocks.prompt: Why does `low <= high` matter in a closed-range search?
choices: It lets one remaining item still be checked
blocks.why: When low equals high, there is exactly one candidate left. It still deserves a check.
